sections.h2: Who sets the value and who sends the bill in Clark County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Two offices do the bulk of the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns each parcel its assessed value, and the sheriff mails and collects the bill starting around October 1. The county clerk steps in after April 15 for anything left unpaid. The sheriff's own page says the office never puts a value on property: your bill is the PVA's value multiplied by the rate for each taxing body covering the parcel, such as the state, the county, a school district or a special district.

The county sits next to Lexington and belongs to its metropolitan area. It covers 255 square miles, and Winchester serves as both seat and sole city. If your house is inside Winchester, ask the city whether it bills a separate city tax and when. The 2020 census counted 36,972 residents, which gives Clark a bigger and more urban tax base than the mountain counties to its east.

sections.h2: Where can I pay a Clark County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Clark County Sheriff's Office takes payment by several routes, and its 2025 taxpayer notice laid them out. The sheriff's office is in the basement of the Governor James Clark Judicial Building in Winchester, and the phone number for questions is (859) 744-4390.

Ways to pay the Clark County sheriff, from the 2025 County Taxpayer's Notice
MethodDetails in the notice
By mailCheck or money order to 17 Cleveland Avenue, Winchester, KY 40391; the USPS postmark counts, private meters do not
Drop boxCheck or money order in the box off West Broadway, with the bill number, map number or address written on it
OnlineDebit, credit or Google Pay through the sheriff's website, with merchant fees
In personCheck, money order or cash; cards with fees; weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm
Bank counterA downtown bank branch on West Broadway takes checks and money orders for the exact amount, with the bill, and no cash

If a bill has not reached you by October 15, call the sheriff. A buyer or mortgage company that should pay it needs the bill forwarded right away.

sections.h2: What are the Clark County due dates and penalties?
sections.html:
They are the same dates every year, set by KRS 134.015 and printed in the sheriff's notice. Use them as a recurring calendar rather than a one-time list.

  • Through November 1: pay in full and take a 2 percent discount.
  • Late autumn through year end (November 2 to December 31): the bill as printed.
  • Every day in January: 5 percent is added.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on.

The county clerk takes over whatever is still unpaid when business closes on April 15. The sheriff's notice warns that payments at the clerk's office carry a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and monthly interest of 1 percent, and that delinquent bills can be sold to a third party. The county's own FAQ says the same: bills go out October 1, the face amount ends December 31, and collection passes to the clerk after April 15.

sections.h2: What do sellers find in Clark County?
sections.html:
An old settlement with in-town houses and working farms side by side. Records show settlers here as early as 1753, and the county was cut from Bourbon and Fayette in 1792. Railroads arrived in 1873 and the early 1880s, and once I-64 met the Mountain Parkway near Winchester in the 1960s, manufacturing moved in around the city.

The 2020 census found 14,917 households and 16,116 housing units. About 65.6 percent of occupied homes were owned and 34.4 percent rented, with 7.4 percent of units vacant and a median age of 41.5. The census counted about 71 percent of residents in urban areas, and the rest in rural parts of the county, where acreage and farm parcels change hands.

  • The Kentucky River, Red River, Lulbegrud Creek and Boone's Creek cross the county, so parcels near the water deserve a look at flood risk before you list.
  • Tobacco and livestock remain farm products across the rolling terrain.
  • Beer cheese began here, and Winchester hosts a yearly festival for it.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Clark County assessed value?
sections.html:
Phone the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250 and ask for a conference before the public review of the roll ends. The review lasts thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and a conference is the required first step. You may hold it by phone.

Still unhappy afterward? Put a written petition in the clerk's hands by the next workday after the review closes, naming the parcel, your reasons and your estimate of fair cash value. A hearing follows roughly a month later. The board expects facts, such as sale listings, construction costs or loan papers.

Officials can also start a review. The county judge/executive, a mayor or a school superintendent may ask the board in writing to look at specific parcels, which is how some values rise without the owner filing anything. The plain plan: confer, file, bring comparable sales and pay on the figure you claim.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption apply in Clark County?
sections.html:
An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can have a set sum removed from the home's assessed value. The state figure was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and a fresh amount is published every second year. A home assessed at $210,000 would be taxed as though it were worth $160,900.

File with the Clark County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shows age. Disability claims require a federal or retirement system classification, and most renew yearly.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Clark County house with unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Title companies pay the balance at the closing table out of your price. Ask the sheriff what the current bill stands at, and ask the clerk whether an earlier bill turned into a certificate of delinquency. Under KRS 134.015 the lien from an unpaid year stays with the land for eleven years whoever owns it, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

Clearing the balance before April 15 is cheapest, because the sheriff holds the bill and extras stop at the penalty and add-on. Afterward the clerk's percentages stack up, and an outside investor can buy the claim. An empty, inherited or run-down house can still sell to an investor who accepts it unrepaired and pays the tax out of the price. Ask for that payoff to be shown as its own line on the settlement statement.

At closing, ask the agent to divide the current year by the date the deed transfers, so each side covers its own months.

faqs.q: Which Clark County phone numbers cover tax bills and values?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff's office at (859) 744-4390 for bill and payment questions. For value questions call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250.

faqs.q: When do Clark County bills get mailed?
faqs.a: Around October 1 each year. The 2025 notice said bills would go out September 30 and appear online, and that owners without a printed bill by October 15 should call.

faqs.q: Does the Clark County sheriff accept cash?
faqs.a: Yes, at the sheriff's office counter in Winchester. The downtown bank location listed in the 2025 notice does not accept cash.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Clark County home for tax?
faqs.a: The Clark County PVA, not the sheriff. The sheriff only collects the bill that results from the PVA's assessment and the local tax rates.

faqs.q: What if I miss the April 15 date in Clark County?
faqs.a: The unpaid bill transfers to the county clerk. There a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and 1 percent interest per month apply, and the bill can be sold to a third party.
